record.paper_title: A Survey on Offline Reinforcement Learning: Taxonomy, Review, and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can offline reinforcement learning be made safe in safety-critical applications not only by avoiding out-of-distribution states and actions, but also by avoiding unsafe states that are already present inside the training distribution, for example through explicitly risk-averse objectives such as conditional value-at-risk?

evidence.quote: Safety-critical RL is also an area we wish to see more people tackle and benchmark in the future. Strategies like uncertainty estimation and regularization have been used to avoid OOD states, but a few works take into account avoiding safety-critical in-distribution states. Toward this end, some works [86] use a conditional value-at-risk (CVaR [87]) objective to learn a risk-averse policy.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a Markov decision process (MDP) M = (S, A, P, r, γ) with state space S, action space A, transition kernel P, reward function r, and discount factor γ ∈ (0,1). In the offline reinforcement learning setting, a learner is given only a static dataset D = {(s_i, a_i, r_i, s'_i)} of transitions collected by some (unknown) behavior policy μ, and may not interact with the environment.

For a policy π, let Z^π(s,a) = Σ_{t≥0} γ^t r(s_t, a_t) (with s_0 = s, a_0 = a, a_t ∼ π(·|s_t), s_{t+1} ∼ P(·|s_t,a_t)) denote the random discounted return. For α ∈ (0,1], the conditional value-at-risk at level α is
  CVaR_α(Z) = E[ Z | Z ≤ VaR_α(Z) ],
where VaR_α(Z) = sup{ z : Pr(Z ≤ z) ≤ α }.

Designate a (possibly unknown) subset S_unsafe ⊂ S of "unsafe" states, which may have nonzero probability under the data distribution induced by μ.

Design an offline reinforcement learning algorithm that produces a policy π̂ from D such that:
(i) π̂ approximately maximizes a risk-averse objective J_α(π) = E_{s ∼ ρ_0}[ CVaR_α(Z^π(s, π(s))) ] for a prescribed risk level α;
(ii) π̂ avoids out-of-distribution state–action pairs relative to the support of D (no extrapolation error on unseen actions); and
(iii) π̂ simultaneously avoids visiting in-distribution unsafe states in S_unsafe with high probability.

Provide finite-sample or asymptotic guarantees relating the suboptimality of π̂ with respect to J_α and the probability of visiting S_unsafe to properties of D (e.g., coverage of μ) and α.
artifact.status_search_result: Several recent works partially address this problem. Offline Risk-Averse Actor-Critic (O-RAAC) and Conservative Offline Distributional Actor-Critic (CODAC) learn CVaR-optimal policies from offline data by combining distributional critics with offline RL constraints (BCQ/CQL). Subsequent work (uncertainty-aware distributional offline RL, spectral risk-measure actor-critic, diffusion-based risk-averse policy modeling) extends this to handle both epistemic uncertainty and environmental stochasticity. However, fully general algorithms with formal guarantees that jointly avoid OOD actions and in-distribution unsafe states under CVaR criteria remain an active research area.

status_evidence.title: Risk-Averse Offline Reinforcement Learning
status_evidence.snippet: O-RAAC is a model-free RL algorithm that is able to learn risk-averse policies in a fully offline setting.
status_evidence.claim: CVaR-based offline RL has been partially solved via O-RAAC.

status_evidence.title: Conservative Offline Distributional Reinforcement Learning
status_evidence.snippet: CODAC extends CQL with a distributional critic and learns risk-averse policies using the return-distribution.
status_evidence.claim: CODAC addresses risk-averse offline RL via distributional CQL.

status_evidence.title: Uncertainty-aware Distributional Offline Reinforcement Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Simultaneously addresses epistemic uncertainty and environmental stochasticity in offline RL.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to extend risk-averse offline RL.

status_evidence.title: Risk-sensitive Actor-Critic with Static Spectral Risk Measures
status_evidence.snippet: Risk-sensitive actor-critic for online and offline RL under spectral risk measures.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizations beyond CVaR are being developed.
